name: DAZN
note: Global broadcaster of the FIFA Club World Cup 2025 (reported US$1bn rights deal). SURJ/PIF took a reported minority stake in DAZN. DAZN's January 2025 company update names Access Industries as its majority shareholder (claim dazn-majority-access-industries). Rating note: SURJ Sports Investment, a subsidiary of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (SportsPro, 17 Feb 2025), agreed on 17 February 2025 to acquire a minority stake in DAZN; the joint release gives no percentage (https://dazngroup.com/press-room/surj-sports-investment-announces-investment-in-dazn/). Reports of its size differ: Broadcast says the Financial Times believed it to be less than 5% (https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/broadcast-international/dazn-sells-minority-stake-to-saudi-arabias-surj/5202130.article); Variety says the deal was widely believed to be US$1bn for 10% (https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/dazn-saudi-arabia-surj-sports-investment-1billion-deal-1236311715/). DAZN's own board page lists Danny Townsend, CEO of Saudi Arabia's SURJ Sports Investment, as a Non-Executive Director (https://dazngroup.com/the-team/, checked 2026-09-28). A state-fund executive on the board meets the METHOD.md link test, so DAZN stays unrated until a maintainer rates it.
